title: Alembic Health hosting escape-hatch discovery
summary: Intro discovery to understand Alembic's desire for an 'escape hatch' from public LLM providers and a path to consolidate serving. Main concerns: eval parity vs OpenAI/Anthropic, latency/cost tradeoffs, SOC2 & KMS requirements, pilot scope (hosted -> dedicated -> private). SE to run a small throughput/latency benchmark with Alembic's top 5 prompts on Redwood hosted and a vLLM/TGI single-GPU config.
topics: current stack: OpenAI + in-house vLLM for onprem inference
failure modes with vendor rate limits
next_steps: Redwood: send hosting vs dedicated pricing snapshot and reserved capacity options (Sofia)
SE: run 5-prompt benchmark on Redwood hosted + provide latency/cost per 1k tokens (Diego)
Customer: share representative prompt set and sample payload (Leo)
Schedule technical deep-dive for private deployment architecture (tentative week of Aug 24)
action_items: Sofia Kim: Email pricing and reserved capacity doc, attach compliance pack. due: 2026-08-13
Diego Martinez: Run latency/throughput benchmarks (hosted) with Alembic prompts, include vLLM/TGI single-GPU comparison. due: 2026-08-17
Leo Grant: Upload representative prompt set and 100 sample records to shared S3 (or link). due: 2026-08-13
Marta Ruiz: Provide SOC2 report scope questions and contact for legal. due: 2026-08-18
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Rana Patel (Alembic VP AI), Evan Cho (Alembic Platform), Marta Ruiz (Alembic Security), Leo Grant (Alembic ML)
transcript: 00:00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick intro, I'm Sofia Kim, AE at Redwood — Diego and Priya are our SEs. How's everyone doing?

00:00:12 Rana: Good, thanks — jumping in from Boston. We, uh, have had a rough couple of incidents with provider rate limits so wanted to explore options for being able to run on-prem or at least have a reliable fallback.
00:00:28 Sofia: Totally makes sense. High level — are you currently running primary inference on OpenAI and then fallback to vLLM?

00:00:36 Leo: Yeah that's right. Most prod traffic goes to OpenAI, but for latency-sensitive internal features we run a vLLM cluster in our k8s. The vLLM stuff is... okay, but ops cost is high and model updates are slow.
00:00:54 Diego: When you say ops cost — do you mean people time or GPU spend?
00:00:59 Leo: Both. We've got two engineers full time tuning batch sizes and cache eviction for KV cache. And we're paying for spot capacity which is a pain during spikes.
00:01:12 Priya: Got it. And what are your success criteria for a migration or consolidation? Latency targets, cost, model parity?

00:01:20 Evan: Critical is parity first — we can't tolerate a drop in quality vs OpenAI for our triage assistant. Latency under 150ms for short prompts, and predictable cost. Security is non-negotiable — SOC2, SSO, encryption at rest with customer KMS.
00:01:39 Sofia: Great. So three buckets: eval parity, performance (latency/throughput), and security/compliance. Quick question — how many concurrent requests / qps are we talking on peak?
00:01:49 Rana: Peak is around 120 rps for short-chat style requests, average payloads small, but we have occasional long runs for summarization.

00:02:02 Diego: 120 rps is workable with dedicated capacity. For hosted, we'd look at autoscaling but the unit economics differ. For your long summarizations you may prefer pinned model instances or a separate queue — the runtime can route to cheaper model variants for background work.

00:02:20 Marta: On the compliance side, we need to understand data residency and audit logs. We also use Azure tenant-wide SSO; SAML is required, and we need KMS integration with our HSM for key wrapping.

00:02:34 Priya: We support SAML SSO and can integrate with customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via KMS, and audit logs are available for dedicated and private — we can send the SOC2 spec.
00:02:51 Rana: Do you have customers who have moved from OpenAI to Redwood while keeping parity? Any benchmarks or case studies?

00:03:00 Sofia: Yes — we have a case where a commerce customer ported generative prompts and used our Optimize tooling to match temperature and sampling configs. Performance-wise they matched latency and saw 18% cost reduction after caching and batching changes. We'll share the case study link.
00:03:18 Evan: Curious about the vLLM/TGI side — we run TGI experiments for local inference. How does Redwood play with those runtimes?

00:03:27 Diego: Good question. Our runtime supports model variants and can route to lighter quantized variants. For vLLM/TGI, customers often use them for local proof-of-concept; Redwood can host the same model weights and we can run kernels optimized for GPU. For purely on-prem, we have a Private package that supports bringing your own runtime artifacts and we can help with conversion/compatibility checks.
00:03:48 Leo: There's some tokenization mismatch between our current tokenization pipeline and OpenAI's — will that affect eval parity?

00:03:55 Priya: Tokenization differences are a common source of drift. For parity we suggest: 1) canonicalize tokenization during eval, 2) run a 5–10 prompt baseline to measure exact token counts and outputs, and 3) tune sampling params. We'll help run those evals.
00:04:16 Marta: About security, how do you handle logs and PII? We must be able to redact logs and limit retention to 90 days for some datasets.

00:04:27 Diego: We have per-customer retention settings, redaction hooks, and we can route sensitive requests to Private where data never leaves their VPC. Hosted has an enterprise option with stricter retention and virtual private networking to regional clouds.
00:04:42 Rana: If we wanted an escape hatch — ideally we'd keep hosted for day-to-day speed but have a dedicated pool we could burst to or an on-prem fallback. Can Redwood do that?

00:04:51 Sofia: Yes. You can run hybrid: hosted for general traffic, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable peaks, and Private for URGENT sensitive workloads. Smart routing can failover to a compatible model variant in a different region/provider automatically.
00:05:05 Evan: Is that automatic or a manual policy?

00:05:09 Priya: You configure routing policies. We support region-based, latency-based, and tier-based. We can also do canary rollouts and automatic fallback if the primary endpoint exceeds latency SLOs or capacity.
00:05:22 Leo: About model weights — for Private do we need to provide them? We have finetuned checkpoints on top of OpenAI-ish models.

00:05:30 Diego: For Private, you can bring weights. We help with conversion if they're in a different format. If finetunes are proprietary, you can keep them in your environment and we only orchestrate locally.
00:05:40 Rana: How long would a pilot take? We want a quick MVP — parity eval then a week of smoke testing.

00:05:48 Sofia: Typical pilot is 2–4 weeks: week 1 onboarding + eval, week 2 run benchmarks and integration, then optional week 3 for a dedicated sizing run. For Private it's a bit longer because of infra setup.
00:06:02 Marta: Any red flags on compliance for us? We operate in healthcare-adjacent workflows so PHI concerns are real.

00:06:09 Priya: Our Private deployment meets stricter controls; hosted can be used but we recommend Private or a Dedicated instance behind your VPC for PHI. We'll share a compliance checklist specific to healthcare.
00:06:20 Evan: Pricing: how do hosted token pricing compare to reserved dedicated? We need to model 1M tokens/day at peak.

00:06:29 Sofia: Hosted is usage-based; dedicated is commitment-based with lower unit costs and predictable throughput. We'll send a modeled cost comparison for 1M tokens/day across three deployment options.
00:06:41 Leo: On the technical bench: for vLLM/TGI we benchmark single-GPU latencies — could Redwood provide similar numbers to help us decide if we can collapse the stack?

00:06:50 Diego: Absolutely — Diego: I'll run a vLLM/TGI single-GPU baseline locally and compare it to Redwood hosted performance on the same model family. We'll include end-to-end latency and tokens/sec and break down batching/caching effects.
00:07:04 Rana: Perfect. Also would like to see how Redwood handles sudden traffic spikes and throttling policies. We had a weekend outage from our provider rate-limiting backfill jobs.

00:07:14 Priya: Our platform offers burst capacity and queued background jobs. You can reserve headroom and configure fallback policies to a cheaper variant or async queue for non-latency sensitive work.
00:07:27 Marta: For SSO, we use Azure AD. Is SAML the flow?
00:07:31 Sofia: Yes, SAML and OIDC are supported for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private we can integrate directly with AD via the customer's network.
00:07:39 Evan: Any limitations on model size for Private? We often use Llama-pen sized models but also larger 13B families.
00:07:45 Diego: Private supports a broad range; limits are more about infra sizing. We'll advise on GPU types and node sizes. For 13B you can serve on a single A100/RTX depending on quantization.
00:07:57 Leo: Real talk: what are typical pitfalls when moving off OpenAI?

00:08:02 Priya: Tokenization, sampling differences, and prompt engineering drift. Also telemetry and observability gaps — we help by shipping eval harnesses and comparison dashboards so you can see exact diffs on a per-prompt basis.
00:08:16 Rana: Can you show us the eval dashboard?

00:08:20 Sofia: We have a demo link — not a full-blown deploy for you yet but an example dashboard and a shared deck. I'll send the link after the call. (notes: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/alembic-hosting-proposal.pdf; eval dashboard demo: https://redwood.ai/evals/demo)
00:08:36 Evan: Great. Any legal constraints folks should expect around model IP? If we bring finetuned checkpoints, what's the license picture?

00:08:45 Diego: License depends on the base model. We can annotate the model catalog with license info; for private deployments customers often keep their finetunes private. We'll highlight any restrictions during onboarding.
00:08:58 Marta: For auditability, we need immutable logs and chain-of-custody for requests in case of incident — do you provide that?
00:09:06 Priya: Yes, we have audit logs with request/response hashes, and retention settings. For Private, logs can be routed to your SIEM. We'll include sample log schemas in the compliance pack.

00:09:18 Sofia: Let's recap next steps — I'll send pricing and compliance docs, Diego will run the hosted + vLLM/TGI bench with your prompts, and Leo will push sample prompts to the shared bucket. We'll tentatively schedule the technical deep-dive week of Aug 24. Does that work?
00:09:35 Rana: Works for me. Thanks everyone — excited to see the parity numbers.
00:09:42 Sofia: Thanks all. We'll follow up by Friday with the initial artifacts.
